headline: Netflix defends Beat Luke Littler line-up after amateur row
standfirst: Fallon Sherrock and 15-year-old Mitchell Lawrie were among the 24 challengers, prompting criticism that the show was not truly for amateurs.
body: Netflix defended the line-up for its live darts show Beat Luke Littler after criticism that some of the 24 challengers were too experienced for a programme billed as a chance for amateurs.

The format gave each contestant one leg of 501 against the world champion, with £501,000 on offer to anyone who won. The best-known name in the line-up was Fallon Sherrock, who in 2019 became the first woman to beat a man at the PDC World Championship. Fifteen-year-old Mitchell Lawrie, the reigning world youth champion, was also selected.

Some fans argued that this went against the idea of giving recreational players a shot at Littler. One amateur who had reached the latter stages of the auditions said he felt he had been "taken for a ride".

Netflix said the rules were the same for everyone: the show was open to people aged 12 and over who did not hold, and had never held, a PDC Tour Card. A spokesperson told City AM that the well-known contestants went through the same auditions as everyone else.
The show was broadcast live from Manchester on 30 October.
